name: Exact paired sign test
definition: Discard exact zero differences under a prespecified policy. For n nonzero paired differences let K=Σ_i 1(d_i>0); under independent signs with probability 1/2, K∼Binomial(n,1/2).
variables: d_i matched difference; n positive number of nonzero differences; K positive-sign count
assumptions: Independent matched-pair differences; under the null, positive and negative signs equally probable conditional on being nonzero.
limitations: Discards magnitude information; cannot infer equality of means; zero differences require transparent handling.
failure_conditions: No nonzero pairs or dependent signs
computation: Count nonzero signs and evaluate an exact binomial tail under the stated null; use prespecified alternative.

name: Pearson chi-square test of independence
definition: For a contingency table with r rows, c columns and N total observations, E_ij=R_i C_j/N and X²=Σ_iΣ_j (O_ij−E_ij)²/E_ij.
variables: O observed counts; R,C marginal counts; E expected counts under independence; N>0; r,c≥2
assumptions: Independent observational units, positive marginal totals, sufficient expected counts for the asymptotic chi-square reference with (r−1)(c−1) degrees of freedom.
limitations: Sparse cells may invalidate approximation; dependence between repeated observations is not accounted for.
failure_conditions: Zero expected cells or repeated observations treated as independent
computation: Calculate marginals, expected counts and Pearson discrepancy; apply a justified asymptotic or resampling null reference.

name: Fisher exact test for 2×2 contingency tables
definition: Conditional on fixed margins, P(A=a)=C(R_1,a)C(R_2,C_1−a)/C(N,C_1). A two-sided probability-ordering p-value sums probabilities of feasible tables no more probable than the observed table.
variables: A top-left count; R_1,R_2 row totals; C_1 first-column total; N=R_1+R_2; C binomial coefficient
assumptions: Independent observational units and valid conditioning on margins under the null odds ratio of one.
limitations: Discrete p-values can be conservative; two-sided conventions differ; does not estimate causal effects.
computation: Enumerate feasible top-left counts and sum the hypergeometric probabilities for the prespecified alternative.

name: Classical one-way fixed-effects ANOVA
variables: k≥2 groups; n_i group sizes; N total observations; mean_i group means; grand_mean pooled mean
assumptions: Independent normal observations within and across groups, common positive population variance, N>k; null equal group means.
limitations: Sensitive to unequal variances in unbalanced samples; rejection does not identify which groups differ.
failure_conditions: Zero within-group mean square or unmodelled dependence
computation: Compute between- and within-group sums of squares and compare F against F_(k−1,N−k) under the stated assumptions.

name: Cochran Q test for matched binary measurements
definition: For n independent blocks and k≥3 binary conditions, let C_j=Σ_i x_ij, R_i=Σ_j x_ij, T=Σ_j C_j. Q=(k−1)[kΣ_j C_j²−T²]/[kT−Σ_i R_i²].
variables: x_ij∈{0,1}; n blocks; k conditions; C_j column totals; R_i row totals; T overall total
assumptions: Correctly matched binary observations within blocks; independent blocks; nonzero denominator; exchangeable conditions under the classical null and adequate asymptotic reference.
limitations: Approximate chi-square reference with k−1 degrees of freedom may be poor with few informative blocks; does not identify which conditions differ.
failure_conditions: No discordant blocks or invalid matching
computation: Compute row and column totals and Q; obtain an appropriate null reference and prespecify follow-up comparisons.
